pages.label: October 28 loop
pages.title: Ready for
pages.lede: Confirmed: four 60-minute interviews on the USC campus, 9:30 am to 2:30 pm. Arrive by 9:00 am. Leadership Principles in every round, a technical evaluation in AI/ML depth plus breadth, and an 8 to 10 minute presentation. Follow today in the 7-day plan.

pages.label: Technical domains
pages.title: Explain it
pages.lede: AI/ML in depth; networking, databases, and security in breadth; CS fundamentals, app development, cloud, and hardware as backup. Every question has a plain answer for a non-technical listener and the technical answer an engineer accepts.

pages.label: Leadership Principles
pages.title: Stories and
pages.lede: The 8 principles named for this role come first, each with two stories. Every story has a 2 to 4 minute version, a self-check, and answers to: How would you do this at AWS? What would you do differently?

pages.label: Presentation
pages.title: Quantization,
pages.lede: Your talk: How do you fit a big AI model on a small computer? Five timed sections of spoken cues, a one-page handout, audience Q&A, and a 10-minute practice timer with saved runs.

pages.label: Mock day
pages.title: Mock
pages.lede: Four 60-minute rounds like the real day: two LP questions, one breadth, one AI/ML depth, and one explain-it-simply question per round, with the presentation in one round. No question repeats within a day.

pages.label: Top SA questions
pages.title: The questions they
pages.lede: Each question opens to a one-minute answer, how to handle it live, the likely follow-up, and the trap. Drill P0 daily; open P1 once P0 feels easy.

pages.label: Speaking scripts & coaching
pages.title: Practise your
pages.lede: Complete speaking scripts, short delivery drills, and optional coaching. Start with ERP migration, incident response, deployment validation, and SQL performance.

pages.label: AWS cheat sheet
pages.title: AWS decisions
pages.lede: A prioritized two-week guide: core services, common comparison traps, customer scenarios, and practice drills.

pages.label: AWS architectures
pages.title: Architectures you
pages.lede: Eight reference architectures you can trace step by step, a requirement-to-service guide, service comparisons, and the checklist to close every design.

pages.label: AWS glossary
pages.title: AWS in
pages.lede: Reference glossary and flashcards. Start with the prioritized cheat sheet, then look up services as needed.

pages.label: Look-alike pairs
pages.title: Look-alikes and
pages.lede: Pairs interviewers use to test real understanding: SQS or SNS, security group or NACL, Multi-AZ or read replica. Say the one-line tell, then when you would pick each.

pages.label: Whiteboard
pages.title: Whiteboard
pages.lede: One framework said out loud, six practice designs with the answer hidden until you have tried.

pages.label: IT fundamentals
pages.title: Fundamentals,
pages.lede: DNS, networking layers, TCP and HTTP, encryption, containers versus VMs, SQL versus NoSQL, sharding, stateful versus stateless, and storage types. Short spoken answers, a timer, and an honest self-score.

pages.label: Questions
pages.title: Questions and
pages.lede: Openers, a rapid-fire technical quiz, an LP question randomizer, customer role-plays, and what to ask them.
